oss_reference.provenance: every OSS-side number used below is parsed out of the source text at run time (sha256 + line number recorded in artifacts/xval_m18194/oss_extract.json)
oss_reference.not_runnable_reason: model generator is Python 2 ('from cStringIO import StringIO', Dynamics.c.Rt L51) and the toolchain requires nvcc; neither python2 nor nvcc exists in this environment
oss_reference.decision: Adopt the pressure-evolution + Allen-Cahn h-population formulation as TensorLBM's density-independent two-phase velocity solver IF it passes the two analytic gates below; otherwise reject and record why.
alternatives: A1: keep Shan-Chen pseudo-potential multiphase (src/tensorlbm/multiphase.py) as the only two-phase velocity solver -- it carries a density-based equation of state and cannot give a density-independent pressure field at ratio 1e3
A2: keep the existing conservative Allen-Cahn h-population kernels (tensorlbm.cac_lbm2d, tensorlbm.phasefield.cac_h_population) with PRESCRIBED velocity -- no pressure evolution, no momentum coupling

A3: port the extracted TCLB pressure-evolution scheme (f-population carries p, gbar-equilibrium + MRT with shear-only relaxation; AC h-population with the anti-diffusion term INSIDE the equilibrium) and gate it on analytic references (adopted)
oss_reference.hypothesis: H1: the extracted pressure-evolution f-population reproduces the 2D Young-Laplace law dp = sigma/R for a static diffuse drop within 15% at density ratios 1 and 100. H2: the same f-population recovers the input kinematic viscosity from the analytic Taylor-Green decay rate within 15%. H3: the AC h-population with the anti-diffusion term folded into the equilibrium conserves total phase mass to machine precision (sum_i theta*w_i*(c_i.n) = 0 by lattice symmetry). H4: the Laplace pressure jump is insensitive to the density ratio (the formulation's advertised property) to within 15% between rho_h/rho_l = 1 and 100.

metrics.primary:
Laplace pressure jump dp_meas =

_in -

_out of a static diffuse drop vs the analytic 2D Laplace law sigma/R_eff, with R_eff = sqrt(A/pi) measured from the conserved excess phase area A = sum(phi - phi_l) over the whole box (no free parameter)
secondary: Taylor-Green decay rate of the f-population: fitted nu vs input nu
spurious current: max|u| at steady state, in units of sigma/(rho_l*nu)
structural: pointwise residual between the extracted TCLB formulas and the TensorLBM port on random smooth fields

oss_reference.baseline_control: Analytic references only, because the OSS model is not runnable here: (i) 2D Young-Laplace dp = sigma/R; (ii) exact Taylor-Green viscous decay u = U exp(-nu k^2 t); (iii) exact discrete phase-mass conservation. Control arm: phi_h = phi_l (single phase) where the interface force mu*grad(phi) vanishes identically and dp must be 0.
oss_reference.stopping_rule: a drop run stops when max|p(t) - p(t-500)| / dp_analytic < 1e-3 (steady_state_residual on the pressure field) or at max_iter = 60000 steps; runs that hit max_iter are reported converged = false and their dp is kept but flagged

controlled: drop initialized with the model's own tanh profile phi = 1/2[1 - tanh(2(r-R)/W)]
changed: R in {12, 16, 20, 24} (resolution study at rho ratio 1 and 100)
confounders: discrete curvature of the phi = 1/2 level set differs from sqrt(A/pi) by O((dx/R)^2) -- separated by the R sweep
spurious (parasitic) currents advect the interface and bias dp -- measured and reported alongside dp
the pressure-recovery correction (rho_h - rho_l)(grad(phi).u)/6 is itself velocity dependent, so it vanishes only in the exact steady state
tau interpolation is linear in phi while rho is linear in phi, so the viscosity field is not harmonic at ratio 1e3 -- an OSS-inherited discretization choice, not a port defect

oss_reference.repetition_rationale: The scheme is deterministic in float64 with no random seeds; the sweeps (rho ratio, R, M) provide the repetitions, each row one independent equilibration. Determinism is asserted by a bitwise repeat of one case.
oss_reference.analysis: Per row: err = (got - ref)/ref * 100 with ref analytic; pass iff |err| <= 15. Aggregate: max |err| over the primary sweep. Uncertainty: dp is a volume mean over >= 2e3 nodes; the reported error bar is the standard error of that mean plus the steady-state residual. Sensitivity points: R (convergence) and M (interface width).
oss_reference.safety_resource_limits: each drop run < 300 s on one thread; the whole XVAL is designed to finish inside 10 min wall clock on the local 128-core box via a process pool; nothing is submitted to the cluster unless a single command exceeds 10 min
interpretation_limits: the OSS binary is not executable here, so 'cross-validation' means: structural equivalence against source text + independent physical validation against analytic references; a byte-level run-to-run comparison against TCLB output was NOT performed and is not claimed
static and single-phase diagnostics only; no dynamic test (rising bubble, capillary wave) is gated in round 1
the 2D model is compared; TCLB's 3D counterpart (d3q27_pf_velocity) uses a different pressure treatment and is out of scope
the 15% gate is applied to dp and to nu; spurious currents are reported but not gated (no analytic reference value exists)
